arguments.content:
from rocrate.model import ContextEntity, Person
from rocrate.rocrate import ROCrate

crate = ROCrate()

alice = crate.add(
    Person(
        crate,
        "https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000",
        properties={"name": "Alice Doe", "affiliation": "University of Flatland"},
    )
)
bob = crate.add(
    Person(
        crate,
        "https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0001",
        properties={"name": "Bob Doe", "affiliation": "University of Flatland"},
    )
)

data = crate.add_file(
    "data.csv",
    properties={
        "name": "Data file",
        "encodingFormat": "text/csv",
        "author": [alice, bob],
    },
)

print("Test successful - no error occurred!")
print(f"Data entity author count: {len(data['author'])}")
print(f"First author is Alice: {data['author'][0] is alice}")
print(f"Second author is Bob: {data['author'][1] is bob}")

arguments.summary: Modified the Entity.__init__ method in rocrate/model/entity.py to properly handle Entity objects passed in the properties parameter by routing them through the __setitem__ method, which ensures proper conversion to JSON-LD reference format. Special handling was added for '@' prefixed keys to prevent interference with the __setitem__ restriction.
